concept_name: The Derivative as the Limit of a Secant Slope
source_book: NCERT Mathematics Class 11, Chapter 13 'Limits and Derivatives' — chapter-index scope reference only; teaching, examples and phrasing authored from first principles. NCERT Exemplar consulted for misconception beliefs only. IB DP Analysis and Approaches guide (SL/HL split), AP Calculus AB/BC CED, Cambridge IGCSE Additional Mathematics 0606 syllabus (first-principles absence noted) and A-level Pure Mathematics specifications consulted for COVERAGE SCOPE only (curriculum_tags). HC Verma and DC Pandey are physics-only sources and were not consulted. Second mathematics concept through the pipeline; first to ride the cartesian_plane/secant_line/tangent_line primitive family.

real_world_anchor.primary: A car's speedometer shows your speed at this instant — one moment, not an average over the whole trip.

xq.name: Q's x-coordinate (explore drag only — guided states derive Q from x0+h, never name xq)

hlog.name: log10(h) — choreography convenience, NEVER rendered, NEVER a slider

u.name: STATE_8 dedicated sweep parameter — phi-law: never a slider, never drag-bound

h7.name: STATE_7-only linear h sweep for the algebra ladder (0.800 → 0.020, never a slider) — added Checkpoint B F-6

constraints: x is defined for every real number; the plane's visible frame draws x in [-2.4, 2.6] but the curve (function_plot) is plotted only on x in [-2.1, 2.1] — two different intervals, and no caption may conflate them

h != 0 at every rendered chord — the difference quotient is undefined at h = 0 by construction (engine guard |dx| < 1e-12); the STATE_4 exact-zero vanish is choreography-only and never teacher-reachable (drag quantum 1/80 = 0.0125 >> 1e-12)
chord_slope = x0 + h/2 exactly, recomputed every frame from x0 and h — never interpolated, never cached, never duplicated by a second live readout
tangent_slope = x0 exactly, defined and legal to display at every h including h = 0 — this is what un-strands the STATE_5 comparison
canvas pixels = 80 x data units on both axes (equal_scale, k=80 measured), origin at px (252, 294) — the one scale factor, reused verbatim in every *_expr field

f'(x) = x holds for every real x for THIS parent (f = x^2/2 only); the STATE_8 trace (fprime_trace/marker8/seg_tan) sweeps only u in [-1.6, 1.6] — no narration or label may generalise this to 'every curve has a linear derivative' (false: f = x^3 => f' = 3x^2)

STATE_7's h7 (Checkpoint B F-6) is a STATE_7-only linear sweep (0.800 -> 0.020, never a slider, never drag-bound) distinct from hlog/hz — do not conflate it with the log-decade shrink used in S3/S4/S5

scene_composition._design_note: FIX ROUND 2 (json_author, founder_proxy Checkpoint B F-9, 2026-08-07): dropped the on-plane 'curve_label' primitive that used to sit here ('y = x²/2' at data (2.1,2.52)) — it duplicated the SAME string already shown by the 'fs' formula_box below (also 'y = x²/2'), the exact Rule 34b 'one formula surface per state' violation, and worst on THIS state because S1 is the emptiest frame in the whole concept (nothing else competes for attention). Every other state's curve_label survives untouched: elsewhere the formula_box shows something DIFFERENT (slope formulas, the S4 ladder, the S7 lim ladder, f′(x)=x), so no duplication exists there — this is an S1-only fix, not a fleet change.
scene_composition._design_note_2: FIX ROUND (json_author, founder-caught defect, 2026-08-07): was appear_at_ms:10000 — same instant x0's OWN choreography starts sliding it (STATE_1's variable_choreography below), which is a different event entirely. That gate left P (and its readout) off-screen for the first 10000ms of a 20000ms state while the caption ('The curve, one point'), s1_1's narration ('...one point marked on it — point P.') and the state's whole pedagogical job (a subject for 'how steep is the curve HERE?') all assume P is on screen from near the start. Tried removing the gate outright (P visible from t=0): rejected on pixel evidence — the curve's own draw-in (xdraw: -2.1 to 2.1, start_ms 1500, duration_ms 7000) has not yet reached x=-1.2 (P's parked x0 value pre-choreography) until t=3000ms exactly ( (x0-domainMin)/(domainMax-domainMin)*duration+start = (0.9/4.2)*7000+1500 = 3000 ), so for t in [0,3000) P would render as a dot with a coordinate readout floating in empty space next to (or above/right of) a curve segment nowhere near it — confirmed in STATE_1__dense_t01000.png / t02000.png, a WORSE defect than the one being fixed (a labelled point detached from any curve). appear_at_ms is now 3000 — the exact moment the curve's own left-to-right draw-in sweeps through P's location, so P is never seen disconnected from a curve: before 3000ms there is no P yet (curve alone, matching the opening clause of s1_1 while it is still being spoken), and P pops in already SITTING on an already-drawn stretch of curve (confirmed in STATE_1__dense_t03000.png: the draw-in edge lands exactly on P's dot) — the same 'gate a reveal to when the draw-in physically arrives there' technique this state's OWN curve_label primitive used to use before the Checkpoint-B F-9 pass above dropped it (it appeared at 8500ms, exactly when xdraw finished at 1500+7000 — the technique is recorded here for lineage even though the primitive itself is gone). s1_1 (~4000ms estimated spoken length) is still mid-sentence at 3000ms, so P now appears BEFORE the sentence naming it finishes, not 6s after the whole state has moved on.

tts_sentences.text_en: Here is a curve, with one point marked on it — point P.
A car's speedometer shows your speed at this instant — one moment, not an average over the whole trip.
What single number means steepness at point P?

scene_composition._design_note: FIX ROUND 2 (json_author, founder_proxy Checkpoint B F-10, 2026-08-07): readout offset moved {12,20} → {-104,20} — VACATING the space right-below P (where run_label now sits, see run_label's own note) rather than colliding with it. Text is LEFT-aligned off the anchor (drawPlotPoint textAlign(LEFT,CENTER)), so 'P = (1.00, 0.50)' (~114px at textSize 12) now spans roughly px [228,342] on row py≈274 — grazing but not crossing P's own dot (px 332±7, row py 247–261, an 13px VERTICAL gap from the readout row) and clearing the curve/chord to P's left (nothing else is drawn in that region in S2). Verified against the founder_proxy's own suggested number (report 'e.g. {-104,20}'); re-checked visually post-render (see the Checkpoint-B fix report).

FIX ROUND 2 (json_author, founder_proxy Checkpoint B F-11, 2026-08-07): readout offset moved {12,-30} (up-right — runs straight back INTO the rising curve, the named defect). FIRST candidate {-95,34} (left-and-below) was tried and WALKED across frames per the report's own instruction — it cleared the curve but landed almost exactly on 'sec' (the chord)'s own DEFAULT (unauthored) readout anchor, which PM_labelClearOffset computes as roughly (281,166) in canvas space for S2's h=1 chord (perpendicular escape from the chord's own ~56° pixel direction, biased up-left) — confirmed as a real text-on-text collision in a rendered frame (STATE_2__dense_t08000.png, pre-revision), not a hypothetical. REVISED to {130,45}: pushes the readout PAST the plane's own viewport right edge (canvas x=460) entirely — ink-free by clip-construction (curve/chord/tangent can never draw past x=460, the same technique this state's own chord_dual_label/slope_dual_label already use), so it no longer depends on tracking the chord's own moving default position at all. y=45 clears BOTH 'fs' (bottom edge ~102) and this state's chord_dual_label/slope_dual_label (y 123-159, appearing at 15000ms) with margin, verified in a re-rendered frame. STATE_3 and STATE_9 use a SMALLER y (25, not 45) — see their own notes — because their Q can slide down to nearly coincide with P (canvas y approaching 254), where a 45px offset would enter PM_readoutDangerZones' x-axis band (canvas y 291-314) and trigger an unwanted flip; 25px keeps the anchor under that threshold at every reachable Q position in those two states. The three states are therefore NOT byte-identical on this field — a deliberate, documented deviation from the 'shared offset' default, justified by S2's genuinely different geometry (Q fixed high, never near the axis) versus S3/S9 (Q can approach P's height).

FIX ROUND (json_author, defect 2 MODERATE): was the 'run' vector's own embedded label (drawVector always centers a vector's label on the segment's exact pixel midpoint with no offset control). At x0=1 that midpoint sits only 40px from P's own plot_point marker (radius 7px) — with 'run = h = 1.000' (~100-104px wide at the hardcoded textSize(11)) the text's left half reaches back onto P's dot, confirmed in STATE_2__frozen.png (the amber dot covers 'ru'). Split into this standalone label so its position is authorable independent of the segment midpoint.
scene_composition._design_note_2: FIX ROUND 2 (json_author, founder_proxy Checkpoint B F-10, 2026-08-07): moved UP from below the x-axis (data y=-0.45, ~110px from its own segment — read as an axis caption, the named defect) to data y = x0²/2 + 0.20 (a constant 0.20 data units = 16px ABOVE the run segment itself, genuinely 'beside' it now). At x0=1 that is (1.5, 0.70) → px (372, 238) — inside the WEDGE strictly between the run line (y=0.5, px 254) and the curve above it (y=1.125 at x=1.5, px 204): 16px clear of the dashed run segment below, ~34px clear of the curve above. The chord/secant line at x=1.5 sits even higher (y=1.25 for a convex parabola's chord, px 194) so it clears too. x centred at x0+0.5 (not x0+0.4) to sit closer to the SEGMENT's own midpoint (P to P+1) rather than biased toward P, keeping horizontal clearance from both P's dot (px 332) and the 'rise' vertical leg at x0+1 (px 412) — centred text (~96px wide) spans roughly px [324,420], comfortably inside that corridor. Vacating P's own readout (F-10's other half, see P's design note) removes the only thing that used to occupy the space directly right-below P, so this new position no longer competes with it either. Re-checked visually post-render (see the Checkpoint-B fix report).

scene_composition._design_note: FIX ROUND (json_author, founder-caught defect survey, 2026-08-07): was appear_at_ms:15000 — 68% into this 22000ms state. This state's title ('A Chord Through Two Points'), its always-visible caption ('Two points make a chord') and s2_2's narration ('The chord's slope is rise divided by run...') all NAME the chord well before 15000ms, yet the actual connecting line (this primitive) was the only thing on screen that could BE 'the chord' and it did not exist — confirmed in STATE_2__dense_t04000.png and t10000.png (P, Q, and later the 'run' dashed leg are all visible with zero line connecting P to Q) while s2 is actively narrating 'the chord's slope is...'. Same defect class as STATE_1's P (a primitive gated behind an appear_at_ms that postdates its own caption/narration naming it), found during the STATE_1 fix's mandated cross-state survey. Retimed to appear_at_ms:2500 — the same instant Q lands (Q's own appear_at_ms) — so 'two points make a chord' is true the moment the second point exists (an immediate, direct visual consequence, not a delayed one); the run/rise vectors (7000/11000) now read as a decomposition of an ALREADY-VISIBLE chord's slope into rise/run legs, rather than legs assembling toward a chord that isn't there yet. chord_dual_label/slope_dual_label stay at 15000 unchanged — they are a formal-terminology beat ('chord (secant line)' / 'slope (gradient)') consolidating near s3, independent of when the chord itself first appears, and their collision-safe positions (see their own _design_note) do not depend on sec's reveal time. focal_sequence is unaffected: sec is a visible-but-dimmed peer (alphaMul 0.6) from 2500 until its own focal window opens at 15000, the same 'visible early, glows late' pattern already verified correct for STATE_1's P.

FIX ROUND (json_author, defect 2 MODERATE, second finding): was raw pixel (367,210), inside the P-Q corridor. Verified mathematically against the plane transform (origin px (252,294), k=80): the curve y=x^2/2 and the chord line y=1.5x-1 intersect ONLY at P (x=1) and Q (x=2) — everywhere between them they run within ~10px of each other (max separation 0.125 data units at x=1.5, the corridor's midpoint), far less than a single text line's height, so NO horizontal label can sit inside that corridor without one stroke or the other crossing it (confirmed in STATE_2__frozen.png: the secant line crosses directly through 'secant'). Moved outside the plane's viewport entirely (viewport is x in [60,460] px; CALLOUT_ZONE_R starts at x=475) so neither the curve nor the extended secant line (visible only for canvas x in [201,449]) can ever reach it, mathematically guaranteed rather than nudged-and-hoped. Placed directly below the 'fs' formula box (560,64, ~172px wide, bottom edge ~102) in the same right-hand column, reading as a continuation of that definitions column rather than a floating orphan.

FIX ROUND (founder-caught, 2026-08-07): was raw pixel (382,166), CENTER-aligned (drawLabel uses textAlign(CENTER,CENTER)) so it spanned x 340-424. The pcpl round-2 readout-clearance fix (parametric_renderer.ts on feat/pcpl-readout-placement, b50632e) displaces a secant_line's readout along the line normal by the label's own support function so the stroke can never cross it; on STATE_2 that moves 'sec' readout 'slope = 1.5000' to x 297-375, producing a 34px text-on-text overlap with this caption, confirmed in-frame at 4x. Neither side could avoid the other: canvas-drawn readouts never enter the de-overlap solver (subSimSolverHost.ts) that places label primitives, so no gate could see the collision (filed OPEN/MAJOR as canvas_drawn_readouts_never_enter_the_de_overlap_solver_*). Moved into the right-hand definitions column directly below chord_dual_label (640,130), matching that label's own note ('reading as a continuation of that definitions column'): the two dual-terminology captions now stack as one block, 'chord (secant line)' over 'slope (gradient)', both already appearing together at 15000ms. At (640,152) the text spans about x 596-684, y 146-158 - clear of the fs formula box above it (bottom edge ~102), inside the 760px canvas, and outside the plane viewport (x in [60,460]) so neither the curve nor the frame-extended secant line can ever reach it, mathematically guaranteed rather than nudged-and-hoped. Chosen to be independent of the readout's slope-dependent placement, so no future clearance change can re-collide it.

tts_sentences.text_en: A point Q appears, a gap h from point P.
The chord's slope is rise divided by run — how far the curve climbs between the two points, divided by the gap h.
That is the average rate — not yet the rate at point P.

misconception_watch.belief: Average rate and the rate at a point are the same thing
misconception_watch.visual_counter: the opening dwell shows the h = 1 chord reading slope 1.5000 — if that were the answer, the number would be done; then Q slides and the number keeps moving, settling near 1.0050 — only the settling value belongs to the point
misconception_watch.one_line_fix: A chord's slope is an average over its gap; the point's slope is the number those averages settle on.

scene_composition._design_note: FIX ROUND 2 (json_author, founder_proxy Checkpoint B F-11, 2026-08-07): readout offset moved {12,-30} → {130,25} — pushes the readout past the plane's viewport edge (canvas x=460, ink-free by clip-construction), same technique as STATE_2's Q fix, but y=25 (not S2's 45): this state's Q slides all the way down to Q≈P (canvas y approaching 254 as h shrinks toward 0.01), and PM_readoutDangerZones' x-axis band starts at canvas y=291 — a 25px offset keeps the anchor (max ≈254+25=279) under that threshold for the whole reachable range, so the renderer's collision-flip never fires and the readout never jumps back toward the curve/y-axis side. (S2 could safely use a larger 45px offset because its Q sits fixed at canvas y=134, nowhere near that band; S3's continuously-sliding Q cannot assume that headroom.) Verified in re-rendered dense frames across the FULL sweep including the exact state-end (t=24000ms, Q=(1.01,0.51), h=0.010): no flip fired anywhere, and the readout stays clean and clearly separated from P's own text even as the two dots visually merge — see the Checkpoint-B fix report.

tts_sentences.text_en: Watch the gap, h, shrink.
At gap h equal to one, the chord reads slope 1.5000 — if that were the answer, we would be done.
But as point Q slides toward point P, the number keeps moving, then settles near 1.0050.
That value, not any gap's average, belongs to the point.

STATE_4.title: At h = 0 There Is No Chord
STATE_4._design_note: B-3 (json_author, verbatim as required): focal_sequence window 2 (13500-14300ms) is the INTENDED void beat — the frame should dim uniformly the instant the chord is gone, before the ladder names why. Do not re-time this window to 'fix' it. FIX ROUND (json_author, evidence-based, 2026-08 eye_walker defect 1 MAJOR): the window 2 entry originally carried NO highlight_primitive_id key at all (not 'row5' as an earlier note claimed — that claim was never actually reflected in the authored JSON). PM_focalEmphasis's loop sets focalId = seq[i].highlight_primitive_id = undefined for a keyless entry; the post-loop 'keep last' fallback tests `focalId === null` specifically, and undefined !== null, so that fallback does NOT fire — focalId stays undefined, `!focalId` is true, and control falls through to Priority 2, this state's REQUIRED static focal_primitive_id ('P'). Verified in pixels (STATE_4__dense_t14000.png, pre-fix): P's dot and readout render bold with a visible glow-bloom during the void window — the OPPOSITE of 'nobody glows'. FIX: window 2's highlight_primitive_id is now the sentinel string '__void_beat__', which matches no primitive id in this state's scene_composition. This keeps focalId truthy (so neither the null-keep-last fallback NOR the static-focal fallback fires) while guaranteeing `focalId === spec.id` is false for every real primitive — every visible peer (P, curve, row1-row4, fs) evaluates isFocal:false/alphaMul:0.6/glowPx:0 uniformly, and nothing glows. Re-verified in pixels post-fix at t=14000ms. Note the state's window 3 ('row6', 14300-24000ms) already exhibits this same 'target not yet on screen = uniform dim' behavior for the 3200ms before row6.appear_at_ms=17500 — that sub-window was NOT a bug, since 'row6' is itself a non-empty string that never equals any OTHER primitive's id either, so it never fell through to the static-focal trap; it is the existing precedent the sentinel-id fix now mirrors deliberately for window 2.

misconception_watch.belief: At h = 0 it's 0/0, so the slope at a point is meaningless
misconception_watch.visual_counter: the engine itself performs the consequence: Q lands on P and the chord plus its readout vanish; the ladder rows stay on screen as VALUES (1.2000 / 1.0500 / 1.0050 / 1.0005), then row 5 names the void (h = 0 → no chord), then row 6 names the limit (slopes → 1.0000)
misconception_watch.one_line_fix: h = 0 is excluded; the derivative is the number the slopes approach, not the slope you compute there.

scene_composition._design_note: FIX ROUND 2 (json_author, founder_proxy Checkpoint B F-3, 2026-08-07): text was 'h = 0: no chord' — false for the first 13500ms of this 24000ms state (the chord is plainly on screen and rotating for 56% of the state's runtime; it only vanishes at 13500ms exactly). Reworded to the ACTION the state performs, which is true for the whole state per the architect's own suggested wording (applied verbatim).

FIX ROUND 2 (json_author, founder_proxy Checkpoint B F-4, 2026-08-07): S4 is CORE ring, but its own 'fs' formula box uses the symbols f(...) and x₀ — notation never DEFINED anywhere in the core-only path (S1–S6, S9; the only place x₀ is explained as 'this point's own x-coordinate' is S7's x0_chip, which is ADVANCED ring and hidden under the no_advanced/core_only preset, 38a). Grounds the symbol here with a concrete live number — the exact fix the report suggests ('put S7's x₀ = 1.00 chip on S4') — so a student on the core-only cut can read x₀ off this chip and off P's own readout (already showing '(1.00, 0.50)') and infer 'x₀ is just P's x-coordinate' without ever needing S7.

tts_sentences.text_en: Shrink the gap again and watch each value pass.
Two points become one: no chord, no slope — zero over zero is not a number.
Yet the values were approaching one number: 1.0050, then 1.0005, closer to 1.0000 — the limit, the slope at the point.

STATE_5.title: The Tangent: One Line Remains
STATE_5._design_note: B-4 (mathematics_author's FLAG 1 fix, applied here) split the approved window 3 (sec, 4000-14000) into sec(4000-12800) -> a bridging window (12800-14000, no highlight_primitive_id) -> tan(14000-22000, unchanged) so the payoff pin at 13200ms does not dim one side of the sec-vs-tan comparison. JSON-AUTHOR CORRECTION (evidence-based, not silently applied): PM_focalEmphasis's bridging-window fallback is NOT literally 'no focal declared, nobody dims' as FLAG 1's candidate fix describes. An entry with no highlight_primitive_id sets focalId to undefined inside the loop; that value is NOT the sentinel 'null' the post-loop 'keep last' check tests for, so it falls through to Priority 2, this state's REQUIRED static focal_primitive_id (schema min(1), can never be empty/absent). During 12800-14000ms this state's static focal ('P', deliberately NOT 'sec' or 'tan') is bright and BOTH sec and tan/tan_label sit EQUALLY dimmed at alphaMul 0.6 — still the intended effect (a fair, symmetric comparison during the pin, never one side favoured), just not a literal absence of dimming. Flagged prominently per B-4 for founder_proxy Checkpoint B.

misconception_watch.belief: The chord eventually BECOMES the tangent — h reaches 0
misconception_watch.visual_counter: at the pin the two lines sit under a pixel apart, yet the numbers refuse to agree: chord 1.0020 vs tangent 1.0000, distinct at every rendered instant down to the finest reachable gap
misconception_watch.one_line_fix: The chord approaches the tangent; only the limit IS the tangent.

scene_composition._design_note: FIX ROUND 2 (json_author, founder_proxy Checkpoint B F-13, 2026-08-07): mirrors the S9 h_chip's −0 clamp (abs(v)<half-the-last-digit ? 0 : v) so a float-noise near-zero x0 (e.g. mid-choreography rounding, never a real reachable value here since S5's x0 is static at the default 1) can never print '−0.0000'.

FIX ROUND 2 (json_author, founder_proxy Checkpoint B F-5, 2026-08-07): readout format changed from bare 'slope = {m}' to 'chord slope = {m}' — S5's whole claim is chord ≠ tangent, and the bare 'slope' left the number ambiguous next to tan_label's explicitly-named 'tangent slope = ...'. Authored an explicit readout.offset (now authorable per PR #46, docs/MATHEMATICS_PHASE0_CARTESIAN_PLANE.md Phase-0 ledger item 8) rather than relying on the auto-computed default clearance, since the string is now 6 characters longer: {55,55} moves the anchor perpendicular AWAY from the tangent's own direction (data slope 1 ⇒ pixel direction (1,−1); (55,55) is the pixel-space perpendicular (1,1), so the readout moves into the open region below-right of P that neither the tangent NOR the near-coincident chord ever crosses) rather than along it (which is exactly what a same-direction offset would re-cross). Re-checked visually post-render across the sweep (see the Checkpoint-B fix report).

tts_sentences.text_en: The tangent line appears at point P.
As the gap h shrinks again, the chord rotates toward it — the two lines become impossible to tell apart.
But look at the numbers: chord slope 1.0020, tangent slope 1.0000.
The picture merges. The numbers never do.

STATE_6.title: A Different Point, a Different Slope
STATE_6._design_note: The skeleton's timing table describes a leftover 'chord fades out 0-1500' beat, but this state's own primitives list (mathematics block STATE_6) authors NO sec primitive at all — the chord is retired for this state's story, not faded on screen. Trusted as the more specific, later-authored source; treated as narrative shorthand for 'the chord idea is retired here', not a literal primitive requirement.

scene_composition._design_note: FIX ROUND 2 (json_author, founder_proxy Checkpoint B F-13, 2026-08-07): −0 clamp added, mirroring the S9 h_chip's pattern — guards the ~23ms window mid-sweep where the choreographed x0 floats just below exact zero (drag is quantised to 1/80=0.0125 and never lands there by hand, but the autoplay sweep does pass through it).

tts_sentences.text_en: Drag point P anywhere on the curve.
The tangent line follows, tilting down, then flat, then up.
Each point has its own slope — at the valley floor, the slope is exactly 0.00.

scene_composition._design_note: FIX ROUND 2 (json_author, founder_proxy Checkpoint B F-6, 2026-08-07): to_expr changed from a static literal 0.8 to the new live variable h7 (see physics_engine_config.variables and this state's own variable_choreography below) so the chord visibly ROTATES onto the tangent as the algebra reveals — 'static plane 24s while cue+narration promise a shrink' was the named defect. h7 sweeps 0.800 → 0.020 exactly across the line3→line4 reveal window (13000→18000ms), so the readout marches ~1.4000 → 1.0100 IN STEP with the algebra concluding.

FIX ROUND 2 (json_author, founder_proxy Checkpoint B F-2 P1, 2026-08-07): was 'limₕ→₀ (x₀ + h/2)' — Unicode has NO subscript arrow codepoint, so the h→0 condition rendered as subscript-h, then a FULL-SIZE arrow, then subscript-0: three type sizes glued onto one operator, invisible at 1×, obvious at 4×. formula_box is single-baseline (drawFormulaBox, textSize 14 uniformly for every line — E-1, no engine fix available this round), so a true smaller-font stacked subscript cannot be authored without an engine change. Adopted the report's explicit engine-free alternative instead: spell 'as h → 0' out in plain words with ONE full-size Unicode arrow and zero subscript characters at all — the malformed glyph combination cannot occur because no subscript-plus-arrow construction is attempted. 'lim' stays (permitted advanced-ring notation, 38c); the expression it operates on and the condition it operates under are now both legible words+symbols at a single, uniform type size. Verified at 4× post-render (see the Checkpoint-B fix report).

FIX ROUND 2 (json_author, founder_proxy Checkpoint B F-2 secondary, 2026-08-07): font_size bumped 13→15 — the report flagged the ₀ subscript glyph sitting so low at 13px that it read as a stray comma next to 'x' at 1× ('x, = 1.00'). A larger size does not move the subscript's relative baseline (a Unicode metrics property, outside authoring control) but does make the whole glyph more legible on inspection, the cheap content-level nudge available without an engine change.

FIX ROUND 2 (json_author, founder_proxy Checkpoint B F-6, 2026-08-07): was a STATIC literal 'h = 0.800' — now that the chord's own h7 shrinks live (see 'sec' above), a frozen caption would go stale the instant the sweep starts and contradict the moving picture. Converted to text_expr reading h7 live, 3dp per this concept's h-precision doctrine.

tts_sentences.text_en: Expand the chord's slope algebraically: x-naught plus half of gap h — that extra half is what the gap adds.
At x-naught equal to one and gap h equal to 0.800, this gives 1.4000, matching the chord.
Only the limit, as gap h shrinks to zero, removes that term and names the derivative.

STATE_8.title: Every Slope Collected: a New Function
STATE_8._design_note: FIX ROUND 2 (json_author, founder_proxy Checkpoint B F-1 P1, 2026-08-07): this state used to render two IDENTICAL unlabelled teal dots 32px apart with NO connector, NO number anywhere, and the curve point (marker8) dimmed at alphaMul 0.6 for the entire 24s (static focal 'fprime_head'). Rebuilt around the primitive vocabulary already in the file (no engine change): (a) 'corr_vector' — a dashed vector from the curve point (u, u²/2) to the traced height (u, u) at the SAME u, reusing STATE_2's already-proven dashed-connector pattern; (b) distinct identity per marker — marker8 recoloured to #FBBF24 (the SAME amber every OTHER state's 'P' point already uses, since marker8 plays that exact role here — a point riding the curve; Rule 32d continuity) with an embedded 'point' label below it, while fprime_head keeps the teal 'derivative family' hue shared with seg_tan/fprime_trace and gets its OWN standalone 'height = slope' label (a separate label primitive, not body.label_below, so it can be offset clear of marker8's label even at u=0 where the two dots literally coincide — see fprime_head_label's own note); (c) 'u_slope_chip' — a LIVE 2dp text_expr readout in the instrument column, the same convention S6/S9 use for their tan_label. Also reconsiders the focal per the report's own suggestion: a NEW focal_sequence (marker8 → corr_vector → fprime_head → fs, summing to the full 24000ms) tells the CORRESPONDENCE as a story — the cause (a point on the curve) first, then the link itself, then the traced effect, then the concluding formula — rather than one endpoint sitting bright/dim for the whole state. focal_primitive_id (the required static fallback) now names 'corr_vector' — the report's own diagnosis was 'the correspondence, not one endpoint, is the story'. Also fixes F-17 (ghost_fprime, dropped — see below).

FIX ROUND 2 (json_author, founder_proxy Checkpoint B F-1, 2026-08-07): a STANDALONE label (not fprime_head's own body.label_below) so it can be offset AWAY from marker8's 'point' label — marker8 and fprime_head literally coincide at u=0 (the curve's vertex, where f(0)=0=f'(0)), so two body-centred labels would stack on top of each other for that instant; this one sits up-right of the dot (position_expr offset by data +0.18/+0.15) while marker8's sits directly below its own dot, so the two never occupy the same pixels even at the coincidence point.

FIX ROUND 2 (json_author, founder_proxy Checkpoint B F-1, 2026-08-07): the LIVE number the state was missing entirely — 2dp, the same convention S6/S9 use for tan_label (an at-a-glance instrument during a sweep, Rule 33d), same violet as every other state's tangent-slope readout (a live slope number means the same thing everywhere in this concept). No appear_at_ms — visible from t=0, so the state's re-entry orientation window (first 5s) already shows a real number, not an empty column.

tts_sentences.text_en: Now watch the slope itself, not the curve.
As the point slides along the curve, its slope at that spot is traced as a new height.
For this curve, those heights line up on a straight line — the derivative, collected as its own function.

scene_composition._design_note: FIX ROUND 2 (json_author, founder_proxy Checkpoint B F-11, 2026-08-07): readout offset moved {12,-30} → {130,25}, matching STATE_3's revised fix (see that state's note for the full reasoning — pushes past the viewport edge, y kept small enough to stay clear of PM_readoutDangerZones' x-axis band when Q approaches P's height). This is the report's named WORST CASE: dragging Q toward P (the state's own target manoeuvre) used to park the up-right-offset readout directly on P's marker and destroy Q's own readable x. Verified via a custom Playwright probe driving the ACTUAL rebuilt sim HTML (assembleSimFromSource → SET_STATE STATE_9 → PARAM_UPDATE x0=1.00, xq=1.02, the closest-approach pose reachable under the drag quantum) and a full-canvas screenshot, cropped/zoomed — see the Checkpoint-B fix report for the captured evidence and its result. Known residual: the drag range extends to xq=-1.9 (the curve's LEFT branch, where this rightward-push offset does not apply the same escape logic); the primary target manoeuvre this report names — dragging Q toward P near the default x0=1 — is the one directly verified.

aha_moment.statement: A point has its own slope: you can watch the two-point slopes settle onto it.
aha_moment.visual_confirmation: the chord's live slope readout counts down from 1.5000 through 1.2500 and 1.0500 toward 1.0050 as Q slides toward P

regeneration_variants.label: Same idea, a cubic curve
regeneration_variants.physical_world: the curve f(x) = x³/6 instead of x²/2
regeneration_variants.same_physics: the chord slope still settles onto the tangent slope as h shrinks to zero; only the algebra of the settling value changes (x₀² instead of x₀), and f′(x) = x²/2 replaces f′(x) = x
regeneration_variants.scene_hint: swap every function_plot.y_expr and every chord/tangent expression's x*x/2 for x*x*x/6; STATE_8's fprime_trace/seg_tan (x_expr/y_expr 'u'/'u*u/2') and its concluding formula_box 'f′(x) = x' become 'f′(x) = x²/2'

regeneration_variants.label: Marginal cost from a total-cost curve
regeneration_variants.physical_world: a factory's total production cost as a function of units produced
regeneration_variants.same_physics: the chord slope is the average extra cost per unit over a batch of size h; the limit is the marginal cost at exactly that production level — the same shrinking-gap argument, a different real-world reading of the y-axis
regeneration_variants.scene_hint: relabel the axes 'units produced' / 'total cost'; keep the same x²/2-shaped curve so every taught number stays unchanged

assessment.mastery_definition: A student has mastered this concept when they can compute an average rate of change from two points, state why the chord slope only approaches (never equals) the point's slope as the gap shrinks, explain why substituting h = 0 gives an undefined 0/0 rather than a number, define the tangent as the limit of chord slopes rather than a line through two close points, compute the derivative at a specific point and as a general function for f(x) = x²/2, and recognise that a straight line's chord slope needs no limit at all because it never changes.

questions.stem: A car's position is given by f(x) = x²/2 (in suitable units), where x is time. What is the average rate of change of f between x = 1 and x = 3?

distractor_misconceptions.A: computes the instantaneous slope at x = 1 instead of the average rate over the whole interval
distractor_misconceptions.C: adds the two endpoint slopes together instead of dividing the rise by the run
distractor_misconceptions.D: uses f(3) alone instead of the change in f divided by the change in x

questions.tested_idea: average rate of change over an interval is (f(b) − f(a)) / (b − a), never the slope at either endpoint
questions.parallel_form_stem: For the same curve, what is the average rate of change of f between x = 0 and x = 2?

questions.stem: As the gap h shrinks toward zero, the chord slope at x₀ = 1 for f(x) = x²/2 …

options.A: approaches 1, but never equals 1 at any h > 0
options.B: reaches exactly 1 once h is small enough
options.C: stays fixed at 1.5 no matter how small h gets
options.D: grows without bound as h shrinks

distractor_misconceptions.B: treats approaching a limit as eventually arriving at it — mistakes the settling value for a value the chord itself reaches
distractor_misconceptions.C: confuses the STARTING chord slope, at h = 1, with the number it is settling toward
distractor_misconceptions.D: assumes shrinking the gap makes the slope blow up rather than settle

questions.tested_idea: a limit is the value a sequence of chord slopes approaches, never a value any single finite chord slope equals
questions.parallel_form_stem: As the gap h shrinks toward zero, the chord slope at x₀ = 2 for the same curve …

questions.stem: Substituting h = 0 directly into (f(x₀+h) − f(x₀)) / h gives …

options.D: infinity, because dividing by zero always gives infinity

distractor_misconceptions.A: reads only the numerator going to 0 and ignores that the denominator does too
distractor_misconceptions.C: conflates the undefined quotient at h = 0 with the limit definition, which is a different number reached only as h approaches 0
distractor_misconceptions.D: applies a 'divide by zero gives infinity' rule from a case where the numerator stays nonzero, which does not apply here

questions.tested_idea: h = 0 makes the difference quotient 0/0, an undefined expression distinct from both 0 and infinity
questions.parallel_form_stem: Substituting h = 0 directly into the same difference quotient at a different x₀ gives …

questions.stem: The tangent line to a curve at point P is best described as …

options.A: the line through P and the very next nearby point on the curve
options.B: the line whose slope is the limit of the chord slopes as the second point approaches P
options.C: any line that touches the curve at exactly one point
options.D: the line connecting P to the origin

distractor_misconceptions.A: imagines a 'next' point sitting right beside P, as if a chord could reach h = 0
distractor_misconceptions.C: uses a geometric coincidence — touching once — that fails to define a tangent for many curves, instead of the limit definition
distractor_misconceptions.D: confuses the tangent with an unrelated line through a fixed reference point

questions.tested_idea: the tangent's slope is DEFINED as the limit of chord slopes, not as a line through two very close points
questions.parallel_form_stem: The tangent line to y = x²/2 at x₀ = −1 is best described as …

questions.stem: For f(x) = x²/2, the slope of the curve at x = −1 is …

distractor_misconceptions.B: drops the sign of x₀, treating the slope as always positive
distractor_misconceptions.C: confuses x = −1 with the vertex at x = 0, where the slope really is 0
distractor_misconceptions.D: reports the y-coordinate f(−1) = 0.5 with the wrong sign instead of the slope

questions.tested_idea: the slope f′(x₀) = x₀ carries the sign of the point — negative to the left of the vertex, positive to the right
questions.parallel_form_stem: For f(x) = x²/2, the slope of the curve at x = 2 is …

questions.stem: For f(x) = x²/2, the derivative f′(x) is …

distractor_misconceptions.B: keeps the square instead of letting it cancel through the h/2 term in the limit
distractor_misconceptions.C: divides by 2 a second time, forgetting the /2 already cancelled in the algebra
distractor_misconceptions.D: treats the derivative as always constant, which is true for a straight line but not for this curve

questions.tested_idea: differentiating x²/2 term by term gives f′(x) = x, valid at every real x
questions.parallel_form_stem: For f(x) = x²/2, what is f′(3)?

questions.stem: For f(x) = 3x, the chord slope between x = 1 and x = 1 + h is …

options.B: it depends on h, as it did for the parabola

distractor_misconceptions.B: assumes every chord slope must depend on h, generalising from the curved case without checking the straight-line case
distractor_misconceptions.C: adds h to the slope, as if the line's steepness itself changed with the size of the gap
distractor_misconceptions.D: confuses a well-defined constant slope with the h = 0 exclusion, which affects only the QUOTIENT, never this line's own slope

questions.tested_idea: a straight line's chord slope is the SAME constant for every h — the settling described in STATE_3 is instant because there is nothing left to approach
questions.parallel_form_stem: For f(x) = 3x, the chord slope between x = 5 and x = 5 + h is …
